harnesses.description: One report per requested harness, in catalog order.

tools.description:
Tools the caller asked about, in request order. Empty unless the
request named tools and a [`crate::ports::ToolLookup`] port exists.

CapabilityReport.description: Answer to the `capabilities` operation for one harness.

discovery.description: Roots the scanner will visit for this harness.

default_install_destinations.description:
Roots an install picker may offer as a destination: the universal
root, plus a harness's own root only when the catalog has it
verified from the vendor's own documentation ([`Confidence::VerifiedFromDocs`]).
An [`RootRole::Own`] root the catalog only infers (Codex's
`.codex/skills`: `docs/action-map/harnesses/codex.md`, "Resolved by
the docs on 2026-09-16") is excluded - installing there would be a
guess about where Codex actually looks.

operations.description: Per-operation support derived from the facts.

observed.description: Machine facts, when the caller asked for them.

runtime_notes.description: Notes for a person (unverified rows, open issues).

AgentIdentity.description:
Kebab-case harness identifier, for example `claude-code` or `open-code`.

Invariant: the string is the serde wire name used by the desktop app
today. `open-code` is canonical; `opencode` is only a CLI binary name and
is never stored in an `AgentId`.

relative_path.description: Path relative to the home or the project.

recursive.description: True when the harness walks subdirectories for `SKILL.md`.

oneOf.description: Under the home root.
Under a project root.

RootRole.description: Role of a root the harness reads.

oneOf.description: The harness's own skills directory.
The shared `.agents/skills` root.
A legacy directory still read for compatibility.
A plugin cache that ships skills.
A root another harness owns that this harness also reads.

Confidence.description: How sure the catalog is about a fact.

oneOf.description: Read from the vendor's documentation or repository.
Derived from a secondary source or an issue thread.
Not found in any primary source.

OperationSupport.description: Support for one core operation on one harness.

operation.description: Operation name, as used in the envelope.

Support.description:
Whether a harness supports one capability.

Invariant: `Unknown` carries no evidence and is never treated as `No`.
An operation that needs a `Yes` refuses on `Unknown` with
[`crate::error::ErrorCode::Unsupported`] and names the missing evidence.

oneOf.description: Supported.
Not supported.
Supported with limits described in the evidence source.
No primary source found.

NativeDisableSpec.description: Native disable facts for one harness.

scopes.description: Scope levels the switch works at.

writable.description: Whether Skill Studio can write the switch safely.

disabled_by.description: Value reported on a disabled deployment.

DisableMechanism.description: Native switch a harness offers to hide one skill.

oneOf.description: Claude Code `settings.json` `skillOverrides`.
Codex `config.toml` `[[skills.config]]`.

`OpenCode` reads V1 `permission.skill` and V2 `permissions[]` skill
rules; Skill Studio writes the V1 `permission.skill.<name> = "deny"`
key (`opencode_config.rs`'s module doc comment has the source
citation for both shapes). `opencode.jsonc` is detected but never
written.

pi `settings.json` `skills` exclusions (`!pattern`, `-path`), also
written by `pi config`.
Skill Studio removes the per-skill link under `~/.claude/skills`.
Skill Studio moves the folder into `.skill-studio-disabled`.

DisabledBy.description:
Why a deployment is off, as shown to the user.

Invariant: the first four names match the desktop wire today; the last
two are new and only appear once the matching mechanism is supported.

oneOf.description: Codex `[[skills.config]] enabled = false`.
`OpenCode` `permission.skill` deny.
The Claude Code per-skill link was removed.
Skill Studio moved the folder aside.
Claude Code `skillOverrides` set to `off`.
pi per-skill toggle.

HarnessObserved.description: Facts observed on this machine, as opposed to documented facts.

config_writable.description: The native config file can be written (parsed and not `.jsonc`).

runner_binary.description: Resolved runner binary, when found on `PATH`.

ToolAvailability.description: Whether one executable was found on `PATH`.

path.description: Resolved path, `None` when the tool is absent.
